newsitem.title: USA: Sheldahl Q1 hurt by inventory, costs.
newsitem.headline: Sheldahl Q1 hurt by inventory, costs.

text.p: Sheldahl Inc said Friday its results for the fiscal first quarter were hurt by adjustments in industry-wide automotive inventories and start-up costs for its micro products plant.
Earlier, Sheldahl reported a net loss for the first quarter ended November 29 of $0.19 a share, compared with year-ago income of $0.12.
Sales fell to $24.3 million from $26.1 million.
Sheldahl said the drop in sales was due to year-end inventory adjustments following an industry-wide automotive inventory build-up in anticipation of prolonged labor disputes.

"Sheldahl's core automotive business was off sharply for the quarter, contrary to our customers' continued forecasts of strong demand in the last weeks of the quarter," James Donaghy, president, said in a statement. "This demand did not materialize. In fact, the reverse occurred. Automotive inventories at both the first-tier supplier and finished parts levels were reduced."
He said customers are anticipating the usual slow December pattern with volume moving up in January.
He reiterated that the automotive business for fiscal 1997 is expected to be down from the record 52 percent growth achieved in fiscal 1996.
"Overall, we regard the recent decrease in sales to the automotive market as an aberration in the growth pattern established by the company since 1989," Donaghy said.
He added that the company's chip-carrier operation is approaching volume production.
"We expect initial engineering qualifications to extend through our fiscal 1997 second quarter, with both sales and production to accelerate during the second half of the year," Donaghy said.
Sheldahl makes flexible printed circuitry, flexible laminates and high density substrates, primarily for sale to the automotive electronics and datacommunications markets.
